1) Section 7 carve: procurement will escalate if we keep any language that could be interpreted as unlimited debugging data retention. Can you confirm the maximum retention window for KV cache drain logs? Is that 90 days? We need explicit days in the MSA.
2) Order form: our finance team asked about prorating for the mid‑quarter start. Is Redwood able to do a pro‑rata first invoice for the partial quarter?
3) PO: procurement prefers to issue a PO and have you countersign rather than DocuSign. Angela — I believe your legal wants a short sample of the final MSA wording before we issue PO.

If you can send a version with the retention window inserted and confirm on prorata, procurement can circulate the PO.

—Samira

Jonas / team — attaching suggested language below; feel free to paste into the redline and send to procurement.

Suggested insertion for Section 7.3 (Inference Logs and Diagnostic Data):
"For the purposes of troubleshooting and resolving incidents, Redwood may retain ephemeral inference diagnostic artifacts (including aggregated model telemetry and KV cache drain reports) for up to ninety (90) days. Notwithstanding the foregoing, raw request payloads and per‑request token level logs will be retained for no longer than thirty (30) days and will be purged automatically unless Customer expressly requests a longer retention window for a specific, documented investigation. Redwood will not use retained raw payloads to improve or train public models. Access to retained artifacts will be limited to authorized Redwood personnel and logged for audit."
On the prorata question: we can issue a pro‑rata invoice for the initial partial quarter; finance confirms they'll accept a PO referencing the final signed MSA + order form and a one‑line invoice for the partial period.

I can add this language to the redline and produce a clean final MSA for signature. Recommend we confirm the PO contact and signature name so Marissa can route countersignature promptly.

Karthik
